statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of six paths/templates. Not covered: authenticated profile/favourites, third-party OAuth completion, destructive account actions, upload after authentication, actual binary download response, and exhaustive item URLs because they require credentials/external identity or duplicate audited templates.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark colour-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The screenshot captured with prefers-color-scheme: dark remains a light #f9fbfe page, and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface and text tokens using the dark-mode guidance.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences are not explicitly supported, and low-contrast text already fails WCAG.
findings.evidence: The preferences probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors CSS; Lighthouse measured the ADVERTISEMENT label at 1.85:1 against #f9fbfe.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors/prefers-contrast styles and raise normal-mode text contrast to at least WCAG minimums.

findings.summary: Route changes use abrupt document swaps with no View Transition enhancement.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition declarations on the multi-page browse and detail journeys.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin navigation with cross-document View Transitions and retain an instant-navigation fallback.

findings.summary: The first visit is interrupted by a modal consent wall that obscures all primary content.
findings.evidence: The initial desktop screenshot shows a large blocking consent panel over the homepage before the user can reach the content.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-first consent surface where legally possible, preserve equally prominent accept/reject actions, and avoid obscuring the core page.

findings.summary: The consent overlay is not exposed through a native dialog or equivalent modal semantics.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection during the first-visit state found zero dialog elements and zero aria-modal elements while the visible panel blocked the page.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the modal with <dialog>, an accessible name, initial focus, Escape/cancel handling, and focus restoration.

findings.summary: Reusable listing cards adapt only through global layout rules, not their container.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container rules even though the same media-card component appears at desktop and mobile widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the card an appropriate containment context and use size container queries for local card composition changes.

findings.summary: Many interactive tag targets are too short for comfortable touch use.
findings.evidence: The focus/geometry probe found 14 of the first 15 focusable targets under 44 CSS px; tag links were about 26px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target boxes and spacing to at least 44 by 44 CSS px where practical while preserving visible focus.

findings.summary: The 404 state is a dead end with no recovery action.
findings.evidence: A real unknown route returned HTTP 404 but rendered only “404 NOT FOUND” and no usable site link.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a branded not-found page with a home link, search, relevant browse destinations, and preserved HTTP 404 status.

findings.summary: Third-party and render-blocking delivery dominates an otherwise fast page.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 718,174 transferred bytes, 642,756 third-party bytes, and parser-inserted CSS plus a script candidate; the script was 605,068 bytes total while the trace LCP was 1.12s.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce consent/ad/analytics payload, self-host or trim font selection, and defer non-critical third-party work; keep only confirmed critical CSS in the render path.

findings.summary: The page ships avoidable JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported an estimated 23 KiB of unused JavaScript, while HAR showed third-party scripts as the largest transfer class.
findings.suggestedFix: Use coverage to remove unused first-party code and conditionally load advertising/analytics modules only when needed and permitted.

findings.summary: Text contrast is insufficient for the advertisement label.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported the 10px #bbbbbb ADVERTISEMENT label at 1.85:1 against #f9fbfe, below the required 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a darker text token and avoid relying on tiny, low-contrast labels.

findings.summary: The content page has no main landmark.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed landmark-one-main and the DOM probe counted zero main or role=main elements on the ringtone listing.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the primary listing in <main> and keep header, navigation, advertising, and footer in appropriate landmarks.

findings.summary: Touch targets do not meet the inclusive target-size/reflow bar.
findings.evidence: At 360x800 there was no horizontal overflow, but the geometry probe measured numerous tag links at roughly 26px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target dimensions and verify keyboard, 200% zoom, and narrow reflow together.

findings.summary: The image listing misses modern responsive delivery.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 10 legacy JPEGs, 10 images without srcset, and 9 below-fold images without loading=lazy.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, supply width-based srcset/sizes, and lazy-load below-fold images while keeping explicit dimensions.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap indexing signals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found no canonical URL; an in-browser request to /sitemap.xml returned 404, although robots.txt allowed general crawling.
findings.suggestedFix: Add self-referencing canonicals on public templates and publish a sitemap referenced from robots.txt.

findings.summary: Rich pages lack social preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The listing probe found zero Open Graph tags; the detail page had useful AudioObject JSON-LD but no evidence of Open Graph/Twitter preview metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate og:title, og:description, og:url, og:image and Twitter card metadata per template.

findings.summary: Security headers are absent and first-party cookies are not Secure.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy; both XSRF-TOKEN and mobcupfm_session lacked Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Set Secure on HTTPS cookies and deploy CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Third-party tracking code loads despite the tested reject choice and dominates network bytes.
findings.evidence: After “Do not consent”, HAR still recorded 18 third-party requests and 642,756 third-party bytes, including Google Ads, Tag Manager, Funding Choices and a Google Analytics collection request.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential advertising and analytics until the user grants the relevant purpose, minimize vendors, and verify rejection with a clean network capture.

findings.summary: Authentication offers federated providers but no phishing-resistant passkey path.
findings.evidence: The login surface exposes only Google and Facebook links; no WebAuthn/passkey registration or authentication UI was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and authentication as a first-class account method, with federated login retained as an alternative.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are not configured.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found HSTS, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy all absent, with no CSP frame-ancestors fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Configure the defensive response-header baseline and test it in report-only mode before enforcement where needed.

findings.summary: HTTP failure pages provide no resilient recovery state.
findings.evidence: The tested 404 returned the correct status but only “404 NOT FOUND”, with no retry, search, navigation, or explanation.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a lightweight, progressively enhanced error template with recovery links and actionable messaging.

findings.summary: Styles are not prepared for bidirectional or alternate writing modes.
findings.evidence: The document correctly declared lang=en, but CSS inspection found no logical inline/block properties and the root had no explicit direction.
findings.suggestedFix: Use logical properties for spacing and positioning, retain a correct lang value, and verify an RTL pseudo-localized build.

findings.summary: Wallpaper assets are inefficiently encoded and loaded.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 10 legacy JPEG images, no responsive srcset on those 10, and 9 below-fold images loaded eagerly.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive AVIF/WebP images and defer below-fold downloads.

findings.summary: Non-essential third-party background work consumes most transferred bytes.
findings.evidence: HAR attributed about 89.5% of transferred bytes to third parties, led by advertising, consent and analytics scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritize or conditionally omit third-party fetches, especially after rejection, and batch any essential analytics.

findings.summary: The third-party budget is disproportionate to the ringtone listing’s user value.
findings.evidence: 18 of 26 requests were third-party and 642,756 of 718,174 transferred bytes were third-party on a simple listing.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove low-value vendors, and load remaining media and scripts only at the point of use.
